text: The 2020 French Open was a major tennis tournament held on outdoor clay courts at Stade Roland Garros in Paris, France, and was the 119th edition of the event. Originally scheduled for 24 May to 7 June, it was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic, first moved to 20 September to 4 October 2020, then later adjusted to 27 September to 11 October 2020. This marked the first time since 1947 that the tournament was not held in May–June and the first time since the Open Era that a major tournament was postponed rather than cancelled. The event was part of the 2020 ATP Tour and WTA Tour calendars under the Grand Slam category and was run by the International Tennis Federation. It included men's and women's singles and doubles, as well as junior and wheelchair tournaments. Qualifying matches for singles and doubles began on 21 September, with the main singles draws featuring 16 male and 12 female qualifiers out of 128 players each. The tournament was the only Grand Slam to retain the advantage set in the final set, unlike the Australian Open and Wimbledon, which had switched to tiebreaks. The men's singles title was won by Rafael Nadal, who secured his 13th French Open title and 20th Grand Slam title, defeating Novak Djokovic in straight sets; this victory made Nadal equal Roger Federer's all-time record of 20 Grand Slam titles and marked his fourth consecutive and 13th overall French Open title, with no set lost throughout the tournament. The women's singles title was won by Iga Świątek, who claimed her first WTA singles title by defeating Sofia Kenin in straight sets, becoming the first player from Poland, male or female, and the first player born in the 21st century, male or female, to win a Grand Slam singles title. Świątek also did not drop a set during the entire tournament. The 2020 French Open was also the 124th edition of the tournament and the last Grand Slam event of 2020. It was the first year with a retractable roof on Court Philippe-Chatrier (completed in late 2019), with plans for a roof on Court Suzanne-Lenglen by 2023, and the first year with evening tennis due to floodlights installed on the twelve courts. Because of the September–October sunset in Paris occurring before 8:00 pm CEST, evening matches were possible, with the first women's evening match occurring during Iga Świątek and Martina Trevisan's quarterfinal, and the first men's evening match between Rafael Nadal and Jannik Sinner, which started after 10:00 pm and finished at 1:26 am—marking the first French Open match to end after midnight. The mixed doubles event did not take place, continuing the trend after the US Open. The men's doubles began on 29 September with 16 seeded pairs, and the women's doubles began on 30 September with 16 seeded pairs. In men's doubles, Pavić and Soares won the title in straight sets after defeating Krawietz and Mies in the final, marking their second Grand Slam title. In women's doubles, Hsieh Su-wei and Barbora Strýcová, along with other seeded pairs, were eliminated, and the defending champions Tímea Babos and Kristina Mladenovic successfully defended their title in straight sets. In wheelchair men's singles, Hewett won the title in straight sets, defeating Gérard in the final, securing his fourth Grand Slam singles title. In wheelchair women's singles, Yui Kamiji won her fourth French Open title and 24th Grand Slam title by defeating Momoko Ohtani, 6–2, 6–1. In wheelchair quad singles, Dylan Alcott defeated Sam Schröder in the opening round, and Andy Lapthorne defeated David Wagner in three sets, with the semifinal results leading to the final. The tournament had a maximum spectator capacity of 11,500 across the three main courts, with 5,000 in each of Court Philippe Chatrier and Court Suzanne Lenglen and 1,500 in Court Simonne Mathieu, while qualifying matches were played without spectators. Spectator capacity was reduced to 5,000 in the main courts on 17 September and to 1,000 starting on the eve of the main tournament due to a surge in coronavirus cases. Players were required to undergo two virus tests upon arrival and stay in designated hotels. The Laver Cup, originally scheduled for 24–27 September, was postponed to 2021, conflicting with the initial French Open dates. The men's singles event began on 27 September with 32 seeded players, and the women's singles began on the same date. In the men's singles, 11 seeded players were defeated in the first round, including No. 4 Daniil Medvedev, No. 8 Gaël Monfils, and No. 11 David Goffin, and 10 seeded players lost in the second and third rounds. In the women's singles, 12 seeded players lost in the first round, including No. 9 Johanna Konta, No. 12 Madison Keys, and No. 15 Markéta Vondroušová, and seven more lost in the second round. Serena Williams withdrew before her second round match due to an Achilles injury. In the men's doubles, only one seeded pair lost in the first round, and six of the remaining twelve seeded pairs were eliminated in the third round. In the women's doubles, five seeded pairs and three unseeded pairs advanced to the quarterfinals, with the final between Babos and Mladenovic and Guarachi and Krawczyk, won by the former in straight sets. The tournament took place across 23 courts, including the three main showcourts: Court Philippe Chatrier, Court Suzanne Lenglen, and Court Simonne Mathieu.

In each match, the Japanese player prevailed; Ohtani defeated top-seeded de Groot and Kamiji beat Van Koot, both in straight sets. The final was played on 9 October between the lone Japanese players in the event. In the final, No. 2 Yui Kamiji defeated Momoko Ohtani, 6–2, 6–1, to win her fourth French Open singles title and her 24th Grand Slam title overall. The wheelchair quad singles tournament began on 8 October with the semifinal round. The field consisted of four players; defending champion Dylan Alcott and Andy Lapthorne received the top two seeds, with the other two players unseeded. In the opening round, Alcott faced wild card entry Sam Schröder in a rematch of the final of the US Open some weeks earlier. Alcott was victorious in two sets. The other semifinal saw Lapthorne defeat David Wagner in three sets, with Lapthorne winning the first and third. The third place match took place between Schröder and Wagner, and was won by Schröder in straight sets. The final was played between No. 1 Alcott and No. 2 Lapthorne, with Alcott winning both sets by a score of 6–2 to capture his eleventh Grand Slam singles title. The wheelchair men's doubles competition featured the same eight players as in the singles event. Houdet and Peifer formed the top-seeded pair, while Hewett and Reid were the second seeds. The other pairings were Fernandez with Kunieda, and Cattanéo with Gerard. Houdet and Peifer were beaten 12–10 on a tie-break in their semifinal by Fernandez and Kunieda, after both sides had won a set each, while Hewett and Reid advanced to the final with a straight-sets victory over Cattanéo and Gerard. In the final, Hewett and Reid won the first set on a tie-break before losing the second 6–1, but finished victorious after the deciding tie-break finished 10–3 in their favour. As with the men's competition, the wheelchair women's doubles event featured the same eight players as in the singles event. Two of the four pairs were seeded: Diede de Groot and Aniek van Koot received the top seed, and the second seed went to Yui Kamiji and Jordanne Whiley. In the semifinals, De Groot and van Koot defeated the pair of Kgothatso Montjane and Momoko Ohtani, and Kamiji and Whiley defeated the pair of Marjolein Buis and Charlotte Famin. The final was played between the pair of de Groot and van Koot, the defending champions, and the pair of Kamiji and Whiley. The Dutch pair took the first set 7–6 in a tiebreak, but the latter pair came back to win the second set 6–3 and force the match into a third. The third set, consisting solely of a tiebreak, was won 10–8 by de Groot and van Koot, completing their successful title defense. The wheelchair quad doubles event consisted of a single match, played on 9 October between the pair of Dylan Alcott and Andy Lapthorne and the pair of David Wagner and Sam Schröder. Alcott and Wagner had won this event as partners the previous year, but chose to partner with different players for this edition. The first set was won by Alcott and Lapthorne, 6–4, but Schröder and Wagner responded with a 7–5 win in the second set. The third set consisted only of a tiebreak, which was won by Schröder and Wagner, 10–8, to capture their second and nineteenth overall Grand Slam titles, respectively. Of the sixteen seeded players, only two made it through the first three rounds and into the quarterfinals: No. 7 Dominic Stricker and No. 8 Leandro Riedi. Stricker defeated Lukas Neumayer in his quarterfinal matchup, while Riedi battled from behind to defeat Alex Barrena. The other two matches saw Juan Bautista Torres defeat Lilian Marmousez and Guy den Ouden defeat Sean Cuenin. In the semifinals, Stricker beat Torres in three sets (with both of his wins coming by virtue of bagels), while Riedi booked a place in the final by defeating den Ouden in two sets. The all-Swiss championship match was won by Stricker, as he defeated Riedi 6–2, 6–4, to claim his first junior Grand Slam title. Of the sixteen seeded players, five made it past the first three rounds and qualified for the quarterfinals. Among them was No. 3 Elsa Jacquemot, who was awarded a wild card into the main competition, but lost to qualifier Renata Zarazúa in the first round; she then entered the Girls' Singles competition. Jacquemot defeated No. 10 Kristina Dmitruk in straight sets in her quarterfinal match; the other matches saw Alina Charaeva upset No. 9 Alexandra Vecic, No. 4 Polina Kudermetova defeat Océane Babel, and No. 2 Alexandra Eala defeat Linda Nosková. In the semifinals, Charaeva pulled another upset by defeating Kudermetova, while Jacquemot defeated Eala. The final was played between Jacquemot and Charaeva, and was won by the former, 4–6, 6–4, 6–2. Of the four pairs that qualified for the semifinals, two were seeded. Only three seeded pairs of the original eight made it past the second round, notably No. 1 Arthur Cazaux and Harold Mayot, who withdrew before their opening match. The only seeded pair to lose their quarterfinal match was No. 7 Mikołaj Lorens and Kārlis Ozoliņš, who retired before the second set began. The No. 8 pair of Bruno Oliveira and Natan Rodrigues qualified for the semifinals, defeating Martin Krumich and Dalibor Svrčina in two sets to book a place in the final. The No. 3 pair of Flavio Cobolli and Dominic Stricker defeated Lilian Marmousez and Giovanni Mpetshi Perricard in a third-set tiebreak to win their semifinal match and advance to the final. In the championship match, Cobolli and Stricker defeated Oliveira and Rodrigues, 6–2, 6–4, to win the title. Of the eight pairs that were seeded at the start of the tournament, two were among the four pairs that qualified for the semifinal round. Notably, the top-seeded pair of Weronika Baszak and Elsa Jacquemot were defeated in straight sets in the first round, while No. 3 Alexandra Eala and Elvina Kalieva were knocked out in the third-set tiebreak of their opening match. The semifinals saw the fifth-seeded pair of Maria Bondarenko and Diana Shnaider come from behind to defeat Jéssica Bouzas Maneiro and Guillermina Grant, and No. 2 Kamilla Bartone and Oksana Selekhmeteva lose in an upset to Eleonora Alvisi and Lisa Pigato. This set up a final between No. 5 Bondarenko/Shnaider and unseeded Alvisi/Pigato, which was won in an upset by the latter in straight sets, 7–6(7–3), 6–4.
